title: The Windows Sound System window and its codec
covers: The eight ports of a Windows Sound System window at its base address, and the CS4231 codec's indirect registers 8 to 31

rows.text: The first four addresses of the window are a read-only board ID register, and the second four belong to the codec.
A read of the first four addresses returns the board ID, 0x04 in its lower six bits.
Windows software that finds the board ID assumes the auto-select register needs to be loaded, and that register allows only certain IRQ and DMA combinations.
A WSS program takes INT 7, 10 or 11, half duplex DMA 0, 1 or 3, and full duplex 0 and 1, 1 and 0, or 3 and 0.
A write takes the DMA channel from bits 0-1 and the IRQ from bits 3-5, a layout no line of the document gives.
The emulator accepts IRQ 5, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14 and 15, and DMA channel 0, 1 or 3, more than the auto-select register allows.
R0 is the index address register: INIT, MCE, TRD, IA4 and IA3-IA0.
IA3-IA0 name the indirect register that the indexed data register reaches, and are read/write.
IA4 reaches indirect registers 16-31 and is available only in MODE 2.
TRD set stops DMA transfers while the INT bit of the status register is set.
MCE must be set to change the sample frequency or the interface configuration, except CEN and PEN; the DAC output is muted while MCE is set.
INIT reads 1 while the part cannot answer parallel interface cycles.
The datasheet gives the INIT bit as read-only.
A write names the indirect register the data port reaches.
A write stores TRD and a read returns it.
A write stores MCE and a fall with a calibration mode set starts a calibration, but a write to I8 changes the rate without it.
R1 carries the indirect register that the index address register points at.
During initialization and power down the register cannot be written and reads 0x80.
An indirect register is reached by writing its index in R0 and then reading or writing R1, and 16-31 exist only with MODE2 set.
A write carries the byte to the register R0 names.
While the part initialises a write to this port returns at once, and a read answers the selected register rather than 0x80.
R2 is the status register: CU/L, CL/R, CRDY, SER, PU/L, PL/R, PRDY and INT.
INT is cleared by any write of any value to this register.
A read of the status register returns its byte, whose bit 0 is INT.
A write of any value to the status register clears INT.
A write stores nothing in the status byte: it clears INT and the three interrupt bits of I24 and lowers the IRQ.
R3 is two registers at one address: a write sends playback data and a read receives capture data.
Reading the capture port advances the byte state machine of a sample, and a status read with a new sample received points it at the first byte.
Writing the playback port advances the byte state machine, later bytes of a full sample are ignored, and a status read with the sample sent to the DACs resets it.
The emulator answers 0x80 on the PIO port: programmed I/O is not implemented and no sample byte moves.
A write to the PIO port changes nothing.
I8 is the Fs and playback data format register: FMT1, FMT0 and C/L choose the data format, S/M stereo, and CFS2-CFS0 with C2SL the sample rate.
C2SL picks the crystal: 0 is XTAL1, typically 24.576 MHz, and 1 is XTAL2, typically 16.9344 MHz.
CFS2-CFS0 select the sample frequency, which depends on the crystal C2SL selects.
FMT1, FMT0 and C/L choose linear 8-bit, u-Law, 16-bit little endian or A-Law.
The same bits choose ADPCM or 16-bit big endian, and 100 and 111 are reserved.
C2SL and CFS2-CFS0 may be changed only while MCE is set.
A write sets the format bits, S/M and the sample-rate bits of I8.
I9 is the interface configuration: CPIO, PPIO, CAL1, CAL0, SDC, CEN and PEN.
Except CEN and PEN, the register may be written only in mode change enable.
CEN enables capture and PEN playback, each may be set and reset without MCE, and PPIO or CPIO moves it to PIO.
SDC forces both DMA requests onto the playback channel, and only playback occurs when both are enabled.
A write sets PEN, CEN, SDC, CAL1, CAL0, PPIO and CPIO.
The write enables playback from PEN and PPIO alone and clears the DMA request when it is off; CEN and CPIO are stored and nothing captures through them.
The write reads only PEN and PPIO and never SDC.
I10 is the pin control: XCTL1, XCTL0, DEN, IEN.
IEN enables the interrupt pin, which reflects the INT bit of the status register and is active high.
DEN adds triangular dither before the ADC is truncated to 8-bit unsigned data.
A write sets XCTL1, XCTL0, DEN and IEN.
The emulator stores DEN in the byte and its only branch tests IEN.
I11 is the error status and initialization register: COR, PUR, ACI, DRS, ORR1, ORR0, ORL1 and ORL0.
ACI reads 1 while a calibration is in progress.
COR is set when the capture data has not been read before the next sample, and the new sample is ignored.
A write to the register is dropped.
The emulator's read of this register answers the ACI countdown and stores no COR or PUR bit.
I12 is the mode and ID register: D7 reads 1, MODE2, ID3-ID0.
ID3-ID0 read 1010 as the codec ID.
MODE2 enables the expanded mode; clear, the part is a MODE 1 look-alike.
MODE2 must be set to reach indirect registers 16-31.
A write sets MODE2, and the four ID bits are read-only.
I13 is the loopback control: LBA5-LBA0 and LBE.
LBE set mixes the ADC data digitally with the data sent to the DACs.
LBA5-LBA0 attenuate the loopback from ADC to DAC by 1.5 dB a step.
A write sets LBE, which enables the loopback, and LBA5-LBA0, its attenuation.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; the generate loop sends the DAC data out alone, with nothing mixed back from the ADC.
The attenuation is stored in the byte, and the sample sent out is the DAC data with no loopback path to attenuate.
I14 is the upper byte of the playback base count: PUB7-PUB0.
A read returns the value written.
The current count registers cannot be read.
In MODE 1 or SDC the register serves both the playback and capture base.
A write sets the upper byte of the playback base count.
The write also loads the current count from both base bytes.
I15 is the lower byte of the playback base count: PLB7-PLB0.
A read returns the value written.
In MODE 1 or SDC the register serves both the playback and capture base.
A write sets the lower byte of the playback base count.
I16 is alternate feature enable I: OLB, TE, CMCE, PMCE, SF1, SF0, SPE and DACZ.
TE set runs the timer and interrupts the host at the frequency in the timer registers.
DACZ sends the playback output to centre scale on an underrun.
SPE sends the ADC data out SDOUT and the SDIN data to the DACs.
A write sets OLB, TE, CMCE, PMCE, SF1, SF0, SPE and DACZ.
The emulator's case stores DACZ and acts on TE alone; the output is zero while MCE is set and the DAC data otherwise.
The emulator's case stores SPE and acts on TE alone.
I17 is alternate feature enable II: four TEST bits, APAR, XTALE and HPF.
APAR holds the playback ADPCM accumulator at zero while set.
XTALE keeps both crystals active, and clear powers down the one C2SL does not select.
The TEST bits are for factory testing and must remain 0.
A write sets APAR, XTALE, HPF and the four TEST bits.
The emulator tests bit 3, not the document's bit 2: setting it clears both ADPCM predictors once, and they adapt again while it stays set.
The emulator's case stores XTALE and acts on APAR alone, and no line of that branch reaches a crystal.
I18 is the left line input control: LLM and LLG4-LLG0.
LLM mutes the left line input to the mixer.
LLG4-LLG0 set the left line mix gain, 1.5 dB a step from 01000 = 0 dB.
A write sets LLM, the mute, and LLG4-LLG0, the mix gain of the left line input.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; no mixer level is updated from it, since the update runs for the AUX and DAC registers only.
The gain is stored in the byte; no mixer level is updated from it, since the update runs for the AUX and DAC registers only.
I19 is the right line input control: RLM and RLG4-RLG0.
RLM mutes the right line input to the mixer.
RLG4-RLG0 set the right line mix gain, 1.5 dB a step from 01000 = 0 dB.
A write sets RLM, the mute, and RLG4-RLG0, the mix gain of the right line input.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; no mixer level is updated from it, since the update runs for the AUX and DAC registers only.
The gain is stored in the byte; no mixer level is updated from it, since the update runs for the AUX and DAC registers only.
I20 is the low byte of the 16-bit timer base: TL7-TL0.
A write loads both timer base registers into the timer, and after zero the timer reloads them.
The upper timer register should be loaded before the lower.
A write sets the low byte of the timer base.
I21 is the high byte of the timer base: TU7-TU0.
A write sets the high byte of the 16-bit timer, whose time base is the crystal C2SL selects divided by 245 or 168.
I22 is reserved: the datasheet gives its eight bits as res.
A read of I22 returns eight reserved bits, whose value the datasheet does not define.
A write to I22 sets bits the datasheet leaves reserved.
The read returns the byte the write stored.
I23 is alternate feature enable III: seven res bits and ACF.
ACF freezes the capture ADPCM accumulator and step size while set.
A read of I23 returns its eight bits, which the datasheet states as res and ACF.
The write of I23 is dropped by its empty case, so ACF never freezes anything.
I24 is the alternate feature status: res, TI, CI, PI, CU, CO, PO and PU.
PI, CI and TI say an interrupt is pending from the playback, record or timer count registers.
PI, CI and TI are reset by writing any value to the status register.
The emulator sets PI on a playback interrupt and TI on the timer.
I25 is the version and chip ID: V2-V0, res, res and CID2-CID0.
V2-V0 read 100 for all CS4231 revisions and 101 for the CS4231A.
CID2-CID0 read 000 for the CS4231 or the CS4231A.
The register holds 0x80: V2-V0 read 100, the CS4231's value, where the CS4231A reads 101.
I26 is the mono input and output control: MIM, MOM, MBY, MIA3-MIA0.
MIM mutes the mono input to the mixer, and with MIM clear MBY should be clear.
MOM mutes the mono mix output independently of the line output.
MIA3-MIA0 attenuate the mono input 3 dB a step when MIM is clear.
A write sets MIM, MOM, MBY and MIA3-MIA0.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; no mixer level is updated from it, since the update runs for the AUX and DAC registers only.
MOM is stored in the byte; no mono output is muted, since the update runs for the AUX and DAC registers only.
The attenuation is stored in the byte; no mixer level is updated from it, since the update runs for the AUX and DAC registers only.
I27 is reserved: the datasheet gives its eight bits as res.
A read of I27 returns eight reserved bits, whose value the datasheet does not define.
A write to I27 sets bits the datasheet leaves reserved.
The read returns the byte the write stored.
I28 is the capture data format: FMT1, FMT0, C/L, S/M and four reserved bits.
FMT1, FMT0 and C/L select the capture format in MODE 2; it may differ from the playback format, but the sample frequency is shared and set in I8.
S/M selects stereo or mono capture; stereo alternates left and right samples, and mono captures the left channel only.
A write sets the capture format; MCE (R0) or CMCE (I16) must be set to modify the register.
A write stores the byte; nothing in it sets a capture format from FMT1, FMT0 or C/L.
A write stores the byte; nothing in it makes the captured stream stereo or mono from S/M.
A write stores the byte whether MCE or CMCE is set.
I29 is reserved: the datasheet gives its eight bits as res.
I29 is eight reserved bits; the datasheet defines no value for them.
A write sets I29's eight bits, which the datasheet leaves reserved.
The read returns the byte the write stored.
I30 is the capture upper base: CUB7-CUB0, the high byte of the 16-bit capture base.
CUB7-CUB0 are the eight most significant bits of the 16-bit capture base register.
A read of I30 returns the same value that was written.
A write stores the byte; nothing in it forms a capture base from CUB7-CUB0.
I31 is the capture lower base: CLB7-CLB0, the low byte of the 16-bit capture base.
CLB7-CLB0 are the eight least significant bits of the 16-bit capture base register.
A read of I31 returns the same value which was written.
A write stores the byte; nothing in it forms a capture base from CLB7-CLB0.
